guide.clip.summary: Play a clip on the robot mentor.

guide.moveTo.summary: Walk the mentor to a spot beside the station.

guide.pointAt.summary: Mentor turns and points at an entity.

ui.formula.summary: Show a short formula on the station plaque.

ui.slider.summary: Give the player a slider bound to a parameter.

ui.hide.summary: Remove a slider, tool, the formula plaque or a bench panel.

args.id: slider param, tool name, 'formula', or a panel key: 'steps:<id>', 'table:<id>', 'chart:<id>', 'note', 'explain', 'values' (a list hides several)

sandbox.open.summary: Hand the station over to free play.

data.scatter.summary: Spawn a dataset as class markers on the grid.

args.points: custom only: rows of [x, z, class, y] (class defaults to 0; y, the height for regression, optional); the game names them p0, p1, … in this order

data.label.summary: Reveal or hide class colours/shapes on points.

data.feature.summary: Name an axis after a feature.

data.normalize.summary: Animate rescaling features to zero mean, unit spread.

data.height.summary: Lift each point to its target value (regression view).

loss.show.summary: Show the loss meter for the current model.

loss.surface.summary: Show the loss landscape as a surface over two parameters.

gd.ball.summary: Drop the parameter marker on the loss surface.

gd.gradient.summary: Draw the gradient arrow at the marker.

gd.step.summary: Take gradient steps; the marker rolls downhill.

regression.line.summary: Place a line with a given slope and intercept.

regression.showResiduals.summary: Draw residual segments from points to the line.

regression.squareResiduals.summary: Grow each residual into a square (squared error).

regression.plane.summary: Fit a plane over two features.

logistic.sigmoid.summary: Show the sigmoid squashing scores to 0–1.

logistic.setParams.summary: Sets the model to a chosen guess without fitting; later logistic actions and fitStep work from it

args.w: number (or w1), default the current value or 0
args.b: number, default the current value or 0

knn.distances.summary: Draw distance lines and rings from the query (circles for Euclidean, a diamond for Manhattan, a square for Chebyshev).

knn.vote.summary: The k nearest vote; the star takes the winner's colour. With weighted: true each neighbour's weight 1/d^power floats over it, the bench shows the weight per class as bars and a table, and the model votes this way until a plain knn.vote.

args.weighted: boolean, default false; false (or omitted) is the plain majority vote and turns weighting off
args.power: number 0–8, default 1; w = 1/d^power (0 makes every weight 1, i.e. the plain majority)

knn.regions.summary: Paint decision regions over the grid.

args.centroids: optional [[x, z], ...]: exact starting centroids (overrides method)

kmeans.assign.summary: Each point joins its nearest centroid.

kmeans.update.summary: Each centroid moves to the mean of its points.

cluster.merge.summary: Merge the two closest clusters; the dendrogram grows a link.

cluster.dendrogram.summary: Show the dendrogram beside the data.

cluster.cut.summary: Cut the dendrogram at a height.

tree.root.summary: Start a tree: every point in one node.

tree.split.summary: Split a node with a plane on one feature.

tree.bestSplit.summary: Sweep thresholds and keep the purest split.

tree.leaf.summary: Close a node as a leaf with its majority class.

tree.predict.summary: Drop a query down the tree.

forest.featureSubset.summary: Restrict a tree to a random subset of features.

forest.grow.summary: Grow several trees side by side.

forest.vote.summary: The trees vote on a query.

boost.residuals.summary: Show the residuals of the current ensemble.

boost.addStump.summary: Fit a stump to the residuals and add it.

boost.weights.summary: AdaBoost: each seed's marker grows with its weight. With round: the weights after that round, a weight tag on each seed, and the round's reweighting on the bench: the stump, the seeds it gets wrong, ε, α = ½ln((1−ε)/ε), w·e^(∓α), Z and the weights after.

args.round: integer ≥ 0, optional; 0 = the even start 1/n. If fewer rounds are fitted, fits up to it (walls appear). Omitted: the latest weights, unchanged behaviour

svm.maximize.summary: Widen the margin to its maximum.

svm.kernelLift.summary: Lift points into 3D with a kernel feature.

svm.kernelProject.summary: Cut the lifted data with a plane; drop the curve back to 2D.

bayes.gaussian.summary: Draw a class's bell curve over a feature.

bayes.likelihood.summary: Read the likelihoods at a query.

bayes.independence.summary: Show features treated separately (the naive assumption).

pca.center.summary: Move the cloud's centre to the origin.

pca.rotate.summary: Spin a candidate axis; show the projected variance.

pca.project.summary: Project points onto the top components.

pca.reconstruct.summary: Lift projections back; show what is lost.

nn.perceptron.summary: Build a single neuron with inputs and a bias.

nn.layer.summary: Add a hidden layer (up to 6). Init 'constant' starts every weight at value and every bias at 0, so each layer's neurons are copies. A bench note, model.params and model.explain show they stay identical, with identical gradients, through training.

args.init: adds 'constant' to the existing scale names/numbers; persists for later nn.layer calls until init is set again
args.value: number, default 0.5; the constant weight (used only with init: 'constant')

nn.weights.summary: Show weights as connection thickness and colour.

nn.forward.summary: Send an input through; neurons glow with activation.

nn.loss.summary: Compare the output with the target.

nn.backward.summary: Pulse gradients backward along the connections.

nn.update.summary: Nudge the weights by their gradients.

train.step.summary: Run training steps for the current model.

eval.split.summary: Splits the points into train / validation / test, with a coloured ring per point and a count chart. seed picks the shuffle (same seed, same split). stratify keeps each class's share in every group. Returns the ids per group and counts per class.

args.stratify: boolean, split class by class so each keeps its share (default false)

eval.crossValidate.summary: k folds take turns as validation; a bar per fold and the mean. With keep, each fold's fitted curve (regression) or score (classification) stays on the floor in its own colour, with mean ± sd

args.keep: boolean, default false, leave each fold's curve or score visible side by side and show mean ± sd (population sd)

eval.regularize.summary: Add a penalty on large weights.

ui.table.summary: Show a table of numbers on the bench (the story's own numbers).

args.title: text
args.rows: list of rows, each a list of cells

ui.steps.summary: Show worked arithmetic, one line per step.

args.title: text
args.append: bool: add to the lines already shown

ui.chart.summary: A chart drawn from the story's numbers.

args.title: text
args.mark: optional index into labels: highlight that bar or point

data.values.summary: Label points with their live numbers. T1, t2: each point's coordinates on PC1 and PC2, from the PCA model

args.fields: adds 't1' and 't2' (read through model.components(p); '–' when the current model has none)

data.table.summary: A live table of points and their numbers on the bench. T1, t2 columns, as for data.values

data.outlier.summary: Add one outlier, marked with the warning marker.

data.scale.summary: Stretch one feature (animated): unequal feature scales.

data.shift.summary: Move all points, or one class: distribution shift.

data.imbalance.summary: Keep only some points of a class.

data.flipLabels.summary: Flip labels (label noise); flipped points are marked.

model.params.summary: Show the current model's parameters, live.

model.explain.summary: The current model's calculation for one point, with its numbers.

measure.distance.summary: A ruler or brace between two things, labelled with the distance.

args.id: optional ruler id, default 'dist' (a second id keeps two rulers)
args.show: bool, default true; false removes the ruler with this id

knn.concentration.summary: Show distances bunching up as dimensions grow (curse of dimensionality).

nn.gradients.summary: Gradient size per layer: vanishing or exploding gradients.

eval.roc.summary: ROC curve and AUC of the current classifier.

eval.threshold.summary: Move the decision threshold; confusion matrix and metrics follow. With the logistic model it also moves the model's own threshold (clamped to 0.01–0.99) and its wall or contour.

eval.calibration.summary: Reliability diagram: the scores in equal-width bins, each bin's mean predicted probability against its observed share of class 1, with the diagonal of perfect calibration and the expected calibration error (ECE) on a meter; a 3D board on the back wall's left half and a bin table

args.bins: integer 1–20, default 5, number of equal-width probability bins [lo, hi) (the last one includes 1)
args.table: boolean, default true, also show the per-bin table with the ECE working

knn.metric.summary: Switches the distance without drawing new lines: halos and the ring<k> (circle, diamond or square), the vote, any distance lines and rings already shown, the regions, predict and explain all follow.

kmeans.seedOdds.summary: k-means++ seeding made live: the chosen centroids drop in; every point gets a tag 'D² … · P …' and a ring sized by P = D²/ΣD²; the bench table lists D² and P with the likeliest marked and ΣD² underneath.

args.first: point id, [x, z], or a list of them (e.g. ['p1','p4']); default: the current centroids, else one random point

kmeans.seedPick.summary: Adds the next k-means++ centroid, either a given point or drawn with P ∝ D² exactly as the game's k-means++ draws it, then redraws the odds for the new set.

args.id: point id to pick; omit to draw at random
args.seed: number; the draw uses a fresh generator with this seed (reproducible), else the lesson's

cluster.matrix.summary: A live table on the bench of the distance between every two current clusters under the linkage. The smallest entry (the next merge) is marked in both symmetric cells, and a foot line names it. It follows every cluster.merge, linkage change and point change.

args.linkage: 'single'|'complete'|'average'|'ward', default the current linkage (changing it sets the module's linkage, as cluster.distances does)

gd.rescale.summary: Rescales one input so the loss surface reshapes (e.g. the ravine rounds into a bowl), animated. The ball keeps the same model (w becomes w/s), its trail is squeezed along that axis, and a bench panel shows the coefficients, curvatures λ, κ and the lr limit 2/λmax before and after.

args.factor: number s > 0 (clamped 0.05–20); the curvature along that axis is multiplied by s². Omit it for the factor that makes κ = 1

gd.restarts.summary: Up to 6 coloured balls rolled at once from the given starts, each with its own trail (full-batch gradient, current momentum). Each ends in the minimum its start leads to; balls that reach the lowest loss glow and are labelled 'lowest loss', the others 'stuck at loss …' or 'flew out'. A bench table lists start, end and loss.

args.lr: number, default the current learning rate
args.clear: true removes the restart balls, trails and table

gd.decay.summary: Rolls the ball with a learning rate that decays from `from` to `to` over `steps` (momentum and mini-batches as set), with the trail and the loss chart as in gd.step, plus a bench chart of the lr per step.

regression.robust.summary: Refits the line under a chosen loss: least squares, exact least absolute deviations, or Huber by reweighted least squares. The earlier line stays as a grey ghost, the line moves to the new fit, each point is labelled with its loss, and a bench bar chart shows every point's loss with the largest marked.

args.delta: number, default 1: Huber's threshold, beyond which the loss is linear and the pull is capped at ±δ
args.labels: boolean, default true: per-point loss labels

regression.weighted.summary: Weighted least squares. Each point gets a halo sized by its weight and a '×w' label, the earlier line stays as a grey ghost, and the line moves to the solution of the weighted normal equations, which params/explain show with their numbers.

args.weights: {id: w} | [w per point, in point order] | 'band' (weight 1/σ², σ = RMS least-squares residual per x band)
args.ids: point ids that get weight `w` (when `weights` is not given)
args.rest: weight of the other points, default 1

boost.loss.summary: Refits the gradient-boosting stumps so far under squared, absolute or Huber loss. Each point gets a tag with its plain residual r and the pseudo-residual g = −∂L/∂F that the next stump fits. A bench table lists r, g and each point's loss, and the point with the biggest share is marked.

args.kind: 'squared' | 'absolute' | 'huber' ('mae'/'l1' = absolute), default 'squared'; the loss each stump fits the negative gradient of
args.delta: number, default 1; Huber's δ, where the pull is capped
args.show: bool, default true; the tags, residual segments and bench table (false: refit only)

ada.candidates.summary: Every stump AdaBoost tries in one round, on the bench, best first: the wall's rule, its weighted error ε and the α it would get. The best is drawn on the floor as a highlighted wall labelled with its ε.

args.round: integer ≥ 1, default the next round (fitted rounds + 1); weights are those entering that round

logistic.penalty.summary: Adds a weight penalty to the mean log-loss (L2 ½λ‖w‖² or L1 λ‖w‖₁, b never penalised) and trains under it from the current model; the S-curve or wall slides as the weights shrink, with a ‖w‖ meter, a ‖w‖-by-step chart and a weights bar chart

args.lambda: number ≥ 0, default 0.01 (or params.lambda); the penalty strength
args.steps: integer 0–50000, optional; exactly this many gradient steps. Omitted: runs until the weights stop moving (λ > 0 always converges; λ = 0 then trains nothing)
args.lr: number, default 0.5 (lowered automatically to a safe rate when extra features are on)

logistic.features.summary: Adds polynomial features with their own weights (starting at 0) and trains, so the boundary curves; on the floor the p = threshold contour is drawn as glowing segments (labelled 'circle r = …' when it is a circle), on a row one cut wall per crossing

args.extra: list of 'x2' | 'z2' | 'xz' | 'r2' (x² + z²) | 'x3' | 'z3' (also accepts 'x²', 'x^2', 'x*z', 'x·z'); [] goes back to the straight boundary. Default []
args.steps: integer 0–50000, default 2000; gradient steps after adding the features
args.lr: number, default 0.5, capped at a safe rate 1/(¼·mean‖φ‖²) because x² and the like are large

foundations.step.summary: One (or more) real gradient steps on the line rule f = w1·x + w2·z + b under the chosen loss of y·f; the working (gradient terms, w ← w − η·∂L/∂w, loss and mistakes before → after) goes on the bench and the line slides. With 'zeroone' the gradient is 0, nothing moves, and the bench and a floor label say why

args.steps: integer 1–200, default 1; more than 1 adds a loss-per-step chart

bayes.logPosterior.summary: The posterior at a point in log space: per class ln P(c) + ln p(x|c) + ln p(z|c) as worked steps, the largest score m, Σ e^(s − m), log-sum-exp and P(c|x) = e^(s − lse); log-score labels by the star, posterior bars that never underflow to 50/50, and a bench chart of e^(s − m)

args.at: [x, z], default the current star (or [0, 0]); moves or places the query star

bayes.calibrate.summary: Temperature scaling P(c|x) ∝ e^(ln joint / T): a reliability table (6 confidence bins: count, mean p and share right, before and after) with log-loss, claims ≥ 0.99, boldest miss and 'calls unchanged' lines underneath; the model's prob, log-loss, posterior bars and explanation use T from then on

args.T: number > 0 (clamped 0.05–50); omitted or 'fit' fits the T that minimises log-loss on the labelled points

code.show.summary: Stand Python code on the board at the back of the floor and run it under the tracer, standing before its first line. Every variable in scope then stands in front of the board as its data structure (an array of cells, a string's characters, a stack, a queue, hash buckets, linked-list nodes, a tree, a trie, a graph, a grid, a heap, a union-find forest, a record, or a box for a number), index variables (i, j, lo, hi, mid, left, right, slow, fast, …) as flags over the cells they point at, and the open calls as a tower of plates beside the board. Adds the bench's controls (Reset, Back, Step, Run, Edit code, Speed) and its Inputs, Call stack and Output panels. The camera frames the board and the scene. Returns the station's state: {step, steps, line, event, done, depth, func, vars, ret, output, error, errorLine}.

args.source: the Python program (a string, lines joined with \n). Standard library only; inputs are its starting globals
args.inputs: {name: value}: the program's starting variables, as JSON (lists, dicts with string keys, numbers, strings, true/false/null). The player can change them on the bench
args.literals: {name: 'python literal'}: inputs written as Python (tuples, sets, dicts with int keys: '{1: [2, 3]}')
args.hide: list of line numbers drawn as blank bars until code.reveal
args.reveal: a number n: only lines 1..n shown, the rest blank
args.views: {name: kind}: how to draw a variable when its shape or name does not say: array, chars (a string as cells), stack, queue, heap (a list drawn as array and tree), forest (a parent list), hash, graph, hide. Names inside objects are 'obj.attr' (q.inbox, self.stack). '*' is every variable not named. At a station other than algorithms, on the main floor, every variable is hidden unless named (their values stay in the bench's call stack); on a floor of its own they are drawn
args.pointers: {arrayName: [int variable names]}: which ints flag which array (default: the usual index names over the one array in scope)
args.controls: bool, default true: the bench's controls and panels
args.frame: bool, default true: frame the camera on the board
args.floor: a floor floor.add laid (its id): the board stands on that floor's back edge and the variables in front of it, apart from the station's own scene; default 'main', the station's floor

code.reveal.summary: Show code lines that were drawn blank; the board's frame follows. Returns {hidden, ...state}.

args.upTo: every hidden line up to n

code.hide.summary: Draw lines blank again (a 'what goes here?' before a choice).

code.edit.summary: Change the code and run it again from the start: the whole source, or one line replaced, inserted or removed. Blank lines below an insert or removal keep their place. Returns the new state (error and errorLine say if it no longer runs).

args.text: the line's new text (with its indent)
args.insert: bool: insert text as a new line at `line`

code.inputs.summary: New input values; the program runs again from the start. What the player's Inputs panel and stage edits send.

code.view.summary: Change how variables are drawn (as code.show's views and pointers) at the current step.

code.step.summary: Run the lit line: n steps forward, each animated (values move between cells, pointers slide, new structures pop in). The player's ▶ Step. Relative to where the player is: after a wait, prefer code.runTo or code.goto.

code.back.summary: n steps back. The player's ◀ Back.

code.reset.summary: Back to the first step. The player's ⏮ Reset.

code.goto.summary: Jump to step `step` of the run (0-based): up to 12 steps ahead are animated one by one, more in one move.

code.runTo.summary: Run until line `line` is about to run for the `hit`-th time, counted from the start of the program (so wherever the player had stepped, the beat lands on the same step), or to a return, an exception or the end. Returns the state plus found (false: no such step; nothing moved).

code.run.summary: Run to the end (or `to` a step), animating every step at the bench's speed; from the end it starts over. The player's ⏩ Run; `toggle` pauses a run in progress instead.

code.pause.summary: Stop a run where it is.

code.speed.summary: Speed of stepping and running (the bench's Speed): 0.5, 1, 2 or 4.

code.mark.summary: Tint code lines (the loop, a base case) on the board; no lines clears.

code.editor.summary: Start (or end) the player typing into the code on the board (the bench's ✏️ Edit code). When typing ends the code runs again (code.edit).

floor.add.summary: Lay another 10 x 10 white data floor beside the station's own, its top flush with it, so a part of the lesson (the code board, a spawned diagram) gets a region of its own while the station's scene keeps the main floor. Entity id floor:<id>. Returns {id, x, z, x0, x1, z0, z1} (station-local).

args.side: left, right, back, far-left or far-right (default right): 10.8 units from the main floor's centre, 21.6 for far-*
args.id: its name (default: the side), used by code.show's floor

floor.remove.summary: Take a floor floor.add laid away again.
